item.title: Mactivity 1.9.2
item.description:
• Much less memory in the background: closing the main window now really frees what drawing it took. In our measurements Mactivity holds about 42 MB after you've closed the window, down from about 70 MB, at no measurable cost in CPU. If the window hasn't been opened since launch, it holds about 20 MB, down from about 28 MB.
  • The main window stays where you put it, after you close it and now after you quit too. If the display it was on is gone, it opens centered on one you have.

item.title: Mactivity 1.9.1
item.description:
• Network interfaces use the whole card: each connection's facts now sit in columns (addresses, network, connection and traffic) instead of one narrow list, and fold to fewer columns in a narrow window.
  • IPv4 comes first in a connection's addresses, then the ones that reach furthest.
  • Checkup opens about twice as fast the first time after launch, here and in its summary on Overview and in the menu bar window: its slowest checks no longer wait for each other.

item.title: Mactivity 1.9.0
item.description:
• A Security page: who can do what on your Mac, in one place. Each change is made in System Settings or the browser, and the page takes you there.
  • Protections: FileVault, Gatekeeper, System Integrity Protection, the firewall and automatic updates, each on or off, with what it protects. Checkup tells you when FileVault, Gatekeeper, System Integrity Protection or automatic security fixes are off.
  • What apps are allowed to do: which apps have Screen Recording, Full Disk Access, Accessibility and Input Monitoring, with Full Disk Access turned on. On macOS 26 also the camera, the microphone, Automation and your folders. macOS 27 doesn't let other apps read those four, so the page says so and links to each list in System Settings.
  • System extensions: network filters, VPNs, drivers and security tools that run with the system's own privileges, what each is, and whether it's on.
  • Browser extensions: Safari's, Chrome's, Edge's, Brave's, Arc's and Firefox's, and what each can reach, in plain words: every website, your tabs, your history, apps on your Mac.
  • Time in calls, on the Devices page: hours in video and voice calls this week and today, by app and by day.
  • Network interfaces, on the Network tab: what ifconfig shows, in plain words. Every connection on your Mac, what it's for, its addresses, router, DNS, speed and traffic, and a hover on each that says what it means.
  • Safer with Full Disk Access: Homebrew no longer inherits Mactivity's access when Mactivity runs it. Every release is now checked so no other program can load code into Mactivity.

item.title: Mactivity 1.8.0
item.description:
• Camera and microphone history, on the Devices page: which apps used the camera, a microphone, recorded the screen or read your location in the last week, how long, and the latest times, with a video call's camera and microphone as one. It comes from the dots macOS shows in the menu bar while an app uses one, and stays on your Mac.
  • On Your day too: "FaceTime used the camera and microphone", with when it started and stopped.
  • Downloads you never opened, in Storage → Clean Up: files at the top of Downloads that macOS has no record of being opened since they arrived, a week ago or more, with their sizes. Nothing goes to the Trash until you confirm. Installers, archives and apps are left out.
  • Lighter still: the new camera and microphone history checks every 10 seconds at about a ten-thousandth of a percent of one core, and reads macOS's record only when something changes.

item.title: Mactivity 1.7.2
item.description:
• Watts over any range on the Battery tab: what your whole Mac drew, display included, on average and at its peak, over the range you pick in the toolbar, from 12 hours to a year. Mactivity starts recording it with this update, so longer ranges fill in over the coming weeks and say since when until then.
  • Energy use by app follows the same range, instead of its own 24 hours / 7 days, and shows each app's average watts beside its share.
  • Power reads in watts everywhere: 0.85 W rather than 850 mW, the way chargers and Apple's specs put it.
  • Figures explain themselves when you hover: power draw and watts, the charger's rating, cycle count, max capacity, disk speeds, today's totals, and why internet speeds in bits (100 Mbps) are about an eighth of what Mactivity shows in bytes (12.5 MB/s).

item.title: Mactivity 1.7.1
item.description:
• Apps with an old updater, in Outdated Software: many Mac apps update themselves with a built-in updater called Sparkle, and older copies of it have known vulnerabilities. Mactivity looks inside the apps in your Applications folders and names any that carry one, with the vulnerabilities and an Open App button, since only the app's own update fixes it.
  • An old Homebrew, in Outdated Software: Homebrew versions with known security problems are named, with the command that updates it.
  • Safer updates for Mactivity: an update's signature is now checked before it's unpacked, and Mactivity only accepts an update list that's signed with the same key, release notes included.
  • Both checks read only what's on your Mac, from a list that comes with Mactivity. Nothing is looked up online.

item.title: Mactivity 1.7.0
item.description:
• Your month and Your year, in History → Looking back: time in use against the month or year before, the busiest day (and month), the apps you used most, the ones new this time and the ones you stopped using, your agents' hours and the project they worked in most, slowdowns, data used and written to disk. Go back month by month or year by year, and share either as an image. Through December it opens on Your year.
  • Notes on your history: add a note to a moment, like "Installed the new driver", from Your day. Notes show on Your day, the Today so far ribbon and widget, and every History chart. Click one to change or delete it. They stay on your Mac until you delete them.
  • Heat by app, in History: the apps that take more of the processor when your Mac is warm than they usually do, from the last four weeks. A Mac that stays cool is told so.
  • Charging habits, in History on a Mac with a battery: how long it sits plugged in at full, how much of its charging happens while it's warm, and how often it runs down under 10%, with what would be easier on the battery. Advice only: Mactivity never changes how your Mac charges.

item.title: Mactivity 1.6.5
item.description:
• Outdated Software, in Checkup: what on your Mac needs updating for security. Homebrew's packages and apps, the Python, Node.js, Ruby and PHP versions kept by pyenv, nvm, fnm, Volta, rbenv, asdf and mise, and the Python and Ruby that come with macOS and Xcode. Each says why: known vulnerabilities, no more security fixes since a date, security fixes ending soon, or a newer version out.
  • Upgrade from Mactivity: Homebrew packages upgrade with one click after you confirm, with what Homebrew will change listed first. A language version that's no longer supported gives you the command that moves you to a current one, since upgrading would stay on the old line.
  • Known vulnerabilities, if you turn it on: Settings → Privacy can have Homebrew check its packages against OSV.dev, Google's open vulnerability database, once a day. Off by default. Homebrew sends each package's name, source address and version; Mactivity itself connects to nothing.
  • An alert when something installed has a high or critical vulnerability, or a language version reaches its end of life: once for each package and version.

item.title: Mactivity 1.6.0
item.description:
• Big files you forgot, in Storage → Clean Up: files of 100 MB or more you haven't opened, changed or added in a year, anywhere in your home folder, with each one's last use. Library, app bundles, your projects and their build folders are left alone, and nothing moves to the Trash until you confirm.
  • Duplicate files: copies of the same file across your folders, matched by their contents, not their names. The copy in Downloads is ticked for the Trash first, and copies that share their space on disk with another aren't offered, since trashing them frees nothing.
  • Cloud folders, sized: how much iCloud Drive, Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive and Box keep downloaded on this Mac, by folder. Remove Download keeps the files in the cloud and frees the space here.
  • More in Shortcuts and Siri: ask how your day went, what's out of the ordinary, how your builds are doing this week, and how long your agents worked. Each comes back as a spoken summary.
  • Interactive widgets: a Stay Awake switch for the desktop, and Today so far opens Your day.
  • Your own shortcuts, in Settings → General: choose the keys for Quick Search, Clean Keyboard, Stay Awake and any page of the app. ⌃⌥K always unlocks Clean Keyboard, whatever you choose.
  • Quiet while you present: alerts wait while you're on a call, presenting in Keynote or PowerPoint, or mirroring your display, then arrive as one notification that opens Alerts. A new startup item always comes through, and nothing waits more than two hours. Turn it off in Settings → Alerts.
  • Compare two Macs, on History: save this Mac's report as a file, open it in Mactivity on another Mac, and see the two side by side: processor, memory, swap, heat, disk writes, downloads and the busiest apps. It's a file you move yourself; nothing is uploaded.
  • The Disk tab's totals add up: Today and 7 days showed 0 B on a Mac that had been running since before the span began, and 30 days and the year left out everything read and written since startup.

item.title: Mactivity 1.5.3
item.description:
• Arrange Overview your way: drag a tile and the others make room as you go. Right-click to hide one or move it to the top, or use Edit Overview… to reorder and switch tiles on and off.
  • The menu bar window too: drag its rows into the order you like, and right-click a row or a section to move or hide it. Settings → Menu Bar arranges it as well.

item.title: Mactivity 1.5.2
item.description:
• Customize, in Settings: pick the metrics' colors (Mactivity, Graphite, or a color-blind safe palette), the typeface and weight of the big figures, and comfortable or compact spacing, with live cards that change as you choose.
  • Alerts and Checkup, redesigned: grouped like System Settings, each item with a colored symbol, and the whole row opens where it happened. Checkup separates what's worth doing soon from what's worth knowing; alert rules are grouped by what they watch.
  • Tables end where their rows do: Projects, Agents, Startup, Homebrew, Simulators and Dev Tools no longer fill the page with empty stripes, and their columns fit the window.
  • The History chart no longer shows another tab's figures for a moment when you switch tabs with the window in the background.

item.title: Mactivity 1.5.1
item.description:
• Devices: a new page with every display, its resolution and size, what it's set to look like and whether that's scaled, its refresh rate and how it's connected; each port and what's on it; the USB and Thunderbolt devices plugged in; and whether the lid is closed. A button opens Displays settings.
  • Your next Mac knows your desk: how many external displays you use, how sharp, and how often the lid stays closed. A Mac that lives closed on the desk and rarely runs on battery gets a desktop suggestion, and the advice keeps to chips that drive all your displays: two on a MacBook Air needs M4 or later, three or more a Max chip.
  • Alerts opens on what went off, by day, with the rules a click away in the toolbar.

item.title: Mactivity 1.5.0
item.description:
• Open to the network, on the Network tab: the ports other devices on your network can reach, by app, what macOS's own are (AirPlay Receiver, with where to turn it off), and whether the macOS firewall is on.
  • New startup items: an alert when something adds itself to start with your Mac, naming the app and what it added, even if it put itself back after you turned it off.
  • Who made what's running, on the CPU tab: each app's developer from its code signature, Apple's and the App Store's, with anything nobody's name is on set apart.
  • Wi-Fi over time: the signal through the day or the week, and how long it was weak.
  • Network changes: each switch between Wi-Fi, Ethernet, Personal Hotspot and a VPN, and each drop, with the data used and the apps that used it most. Drops and VPN time show on Your day.
  • A monthly data budget: set an allowance and reset day to see what's left, the pace you're on, each app's share, and get an alert before you go over.

item.title: Mactivity 1.4.0
item.description:
• Projects has new views, in the toolbar: Servers, Space, Homebrew, Simulators and Dev Tools.
  • Space sizes each project's build folders: node_modules, .build, Cargo's target, Xcode's DerivedData, Python environments, Pods and more. Projects you haven't worked on in two months are marked, and their folders can go to the Trash together, after you confirm.
  • Docker's disk use, while Docker runs: images, volumes, build cache and stopped containers, what nothing uses, and the command that reclaims each, for you to run.
  • Homebrew shows what brew services started: its ports, memory and processor, when it was last busy, and the command that stops it.
  • Simulators lists every iOS Simulator device and Android emulator, what the running ones hold, the ones left running after you closed Simulator, and how much space each takes.
  • Dev Tools shows language servers, file watchers and test runners by project, including VS Code's and Cursor's, finds the ones still running after their editor or terminal quit, and quits them after you confirm.
  • Agent limits: an alert when a coding agent's processes hold more memory than you set, and, if you turn it on, when a session runs longer than you set.
  • Build times leave out the Rust and Go dependencies compiled along the way, Vite's long-running esbuild service, and stray one-off compiles; a build still running when Mactivity quits is kept.
  • Compare in Weeks compares two separate weeks, rather than two that share six days.
  • After updates no longer lists apps you've just installed as updates.
  • "Memory keeps climbing" alerts only when an app goes past what it usually reaches on your Mac, so Safari and your coding agent stop alerting through an ordinary day; out-of-the-ordinary notifications need a figure worth an interruption.
  • Today so far counts your agents' time once when they work in two projects at once, and the widget's alert count matches Overview's.
  • Agent history counts the processor used by the builds and tests an agent runs, and keeps its minutes across a relaunch. Claude Code's worktrees count as their project.
  • Quick Search no longer puts Clean Keyboard first when you type "clean" or "keyboard". Clean Keyboard tells you when it needs Accessibility, with a button to the setting.
  • mactivity day, agents and unusual show the right date outside the Americas, and refuse dates that don't exist or haven't happened.
  • Your day and Agents → This week keep up with today while they're open. The day ribbon is right on daylight-saving days.
  • Control Center's Stay Awake reads off once Mactivity quits.
  • Everything follows the time zone your Mac is set to: history bars stay on the hour and on midnight across daylight-saving changes and in half-hour zones, pages move to the new day at midnight and when you change time zone, and --json and MCP times are your Mac's clock time with its offset.
  • Follows more of how your Mac is set up: its own Temperature setting, 12- or 24-hour times, other calendars in mactivity day, and Reduce Motion. Storage shows folders by the names Finder uses in your language, and sizes are in octets in French.
  • Quick Search finds its actions by their names in your language, ignores accents and full-width letters, and offers Ask for questions in any of Mactivity's languages.
  • When someone else is signed in to your Mac too, their apps get an Other users row instead of joining yours, and their coding agents stay out of your Agents tab.
  • Setting the clock back no longer silences alerts; a build left running over sleep isn't timed through the night; the Network tab's connection reads right on IPv6-only networks and over a VPN; a different disk plugged in under the same name shows its own size.

item.title: Mactivity 1.3.0
item.description:
• New: Flagged by macOS. History shows what macOS itself caught: an app writing tens of gigabytes to disk (which wears the SSD), going past macOS's processor limit again and again, apps macOS closed because memory ran out, and restarts your Mac didn't choose, with what was running just before. Checkup tells you when one happened this week.
  • New: App launch times. History shows how long your apps take to open, each app's history page says "Opens in 1.4s", and Checkup tells you when one gets noticeably slower.
  • Beachballs, counted: hangs macOS recorded for the whole Mac now count too, and Checkup tells you when an app hangs much more than it used to.
  • History → Sleep lists your recent sleeps: when, how long, what woke your Mac, and how much battery each used. Checkup tells you when your Mac drained its battery while asleep.
  • Charger check: plugged in, the Battery tab says whether your charger covers what your Mac is drawing, or that macOS is holding the battery short of full.
  • macOS's own processes say what they're doing, in plain words: Spotlight indexing, Photos analyzing your library, Time Machine backing up.
  • Time Machine: Storage shows when your Mac last backed up, and Checkup warns you when automatic backups stop.
  • Fixed: plugged in but not charging, the battery read "Full" at any level. It now says "Not charging" until it's nearly full.

item.title: Mactivity 1.2.0
item.description:
• New: After updates. History compares each macOS and app update of the last month with the week before it: "Google Chrome 155: Memory 1.2 GB → 1.6 GB (+33%)", or about the same as before. Checkup tells you when an update made something heavier.
  • New: Compare. Put any two days, or two weeks, side by side: time in use, slowdowns, alerts, processor, memory, power, data and disk writes, and the apps that changed most. From Your day's Compare… button, or type "compare" in Quick Search.
  • New: What grew. After a storage scan, Mactivity names the folders that grew most since the last scan of the same place, like "DerivedData +9.2 GB", and opens each on the map.
  • New: Build times. Mactivity times every build by project, from the compilers it sees (Xcode and Swift, Rust, Go, C and C++), and tells you when a project's builds got slower: History → Build times, Checkup, and mactivity builds for your coding agent.
  • New: Control Center controls. Add Clean Keyboard and Stay Awake to Control Center or the menu bar.
  • Battery health month by month: History → Battery health → By Month shows each month's capacity and the cycles it used, and the card shows cycles a month. The forecast to 80% now works from wear per cycle too, so it no longer waits for capacity to move.

item.title: Mactivity 1.1.0
item.description:
• New: Out of the ordinary. Mactivity learns each app's usual day on your Mac and tells you when today isn't: "Safari: 5.5 GB of memory today, 4× its usual 1.3 GB." On Overview, in Checkup, and as a notification when an app reaches 4× its usual day (once a day per app; change it or turn it off in Settings → Alerts).
  • New: Your day. Pick any day on History's calendar and Mactivity tells it as a timeline: when your Mac woke and slept, busy stretches and slowdowns with the apps behind them, unplugging and charging, big downloads, alerts and crashes.
  • New: Agent history. Mactivity now remembers your coding agents' sessions. Agents → This week shows how long Claude Code, Codex and the rest worked in each project, day by day, and what they cost in processor and memory; Your day shows each session on the timeline.
  • New: Today so far on Overview: your day on one line, from midnight to now, with a button into Your day.
  • New: Rewind. Click any bar in a History chart to see the apps behind that moment: what was using the processor at 3 AM, or the memory during last Tuesday's slowdown. Hover to read any bar's figures.
  • Network and Disk show today's totals: received and sent, read and written since midnight.
  • Storage's category legend lists every category, wrapping onto a second line when needed, and Your week's top apps wrap in narrow windows instead of being cut off.
  • In Get Info, the CPU and Memory labels sit centered on their graphs.
  • Each app's history page shows today beside its usual day on your Mac.
  • New in the mactivity command and its MCP server: mactivity agents (agent history by project), mactivity day (any day's timeline) and mactivity unusual (what's out of the ordinary today), so your coding agent can ask what happened.
  • New: Clean Keyboard. Press ⌃⌥K (or View → Clean Keyboard) and every key does nothing while you wipe the keyboard, until ⌃⌥K again, Unlock, or five minutes. The first time, macOS asks to allow Mactivity in Accessibility.
  • Back and Forward between pages: ⌘[ and ⌘] in the View menu.
  • Many small fixes so links land where they point: alerts and Checkup open the right card or cleanup, app names everywhere open their history, Esc closes information sheets, a recording shows in the menu bar window, and the View menu's Stay Awake matches the menu bar's.
  • Settings and the menu bar window, tidied: shortening history asks first, alert rules explain themselves and can be reset, ⌘, and ⌘1–⌘8 work in the menu bar window, and Stay Awake says why it stopped.
  • Ask Mactivity (optional, Apple Intelligence on your Mac) can answer about any day this week and about your coding agents: "What happened on my Mac yesterday?", "What did my agents work on?"
  • New: a Today so far desktop widget, your day on one line, refreshed every 15 minutes.

item.title: Mactivity 1.0.9
item.description:
• New: Your week, day by day. The Your week card on History shows how long you used your Mac on each of the last seven days, with the busiest day highlighted. "Busiest day" now names the day you used it most.
  • The GPU page shows which app is using the GPU most and its temperature, instead of repeating the figures above them.
  • Quick Search (⌃⌥M) opens any page by name: type "stor" for Storage or "bat" for Battery.
  • Your next Mac on a Mac mini, iMac or Mac Studio recommends a desktop (Mac mini or Mac Studio) instead of a MacBook.

item.title: Mactivity 1.0.8
item.description:
• Your next Mac is easier to find: its own card on History under Your week, in Quick Search (try "upgrade" or "new mac"), and in the menu bar window's gear menu.
  • "All clear" in Why is my Mac slow? sits in the middle of the sheet instead of left of center.
  • Polish across the app: empty states centered in every sheet, number columns lined up under their headings, the menu bar's Projects list aligned with full project names, the year calendar fitting small windows, accessory names no longer cut short, steadier layouts on the Sound and Privacy pages, and text sizes that match from page to page (an app's history page is titled like every other sheet).
  • Your next Mac: clearer storage outlook ("About 1.7 TB used in three years at this rate") and tidier spacing.

item.title: Mactivity 1.0.7
item.description:
• New: Your next Mac. From 7 or 30 days of how you use this Mac, a one-page report recommends what to look for in the next one: the chip class, memory, storage, and whether a MacBook Air is enough or you need a MacBook Pro. It shows what gets maxed and when, your average day hour by hour, and the apps behind it, and saves as a PDF. Save Report → Your Next Mac… on the Your Week card, or View → Your Next Mac….
  • VoiceOver names the app a mute button belongs to on the Sound page ("Mute Safari").

item.title: Mactivity 1.0.6
item.description:
• New: What's new after an update. Overview says which version you're on now, with its release notes a click away. It shows once, and not on a fresh install.
  • New: Send Feedback… is in the menu bar window's settings menu too. The email draft includes your Mac's model, chip, memory, macOS version and language, so a bug can be reproduced; you see and edit it before sending.

item.title: Mactivity 1.0.5
item.description:
• The totals in the middle of the Overview rings (Power by app, Memory by app) stay inside the ring at any size, instead of running over it at higher figures like 600 mW.
  • Projects no longer grows the window when Docker containers are listed; the containers table scrolls instead.
  • The Sound page fits the narrowest window: each app moves its output menu to a second line when needed.
  • Why is my Mac slow? and an app's history page stay within small screens and windows, scrolling instead of growing past them.
  • The menu bar window's Projects tab shows each project's full name; the status shortens instead.
  • Settings never grows taller than a laptop screen: the General and Alerts panes scroll instead of running off the bottom.
  • Onboarding stays on screen in long languages: its list of features scrolls instead of growing past a laptop screen.
  • The CPU, Memory, Battery and other pages no longer switch layout when a figure gets longer; the layout depends only on the window's width.
  • The Battery page keeps accessory names readable at the default window size.
  • The menu bar window shows up to four accessory batteries, lowest first, and "+2" for the rest, instead of wrapping.
  • The Battery card's icon shows the battery's level.
  • The license screen's Activate button keeps its full name in every language.
  • Storage fits the narrowest window after a scan; in a narrow folder list, names stay readable and the share bars step aside.

item.title: Mactivity 1.0.4
item.description:
• Mactivity reopens on the page you were on, after an update or when you quit and open it again, instead of starting on Overview.
  • In a smaller window, the CPU, Memory, Disk, Network, GPU and Battery pages scroll instead of sliding up under the toolbar, and the app list keeps a usable height.

item.title: Mactivity 1.0.3
item.description: • Storage no longer slides up under the toolbar during or after a scan, or when you open Space you can get back. In a short window the map draws smaller instead.

item.title: Mactivity 1.0.2
item.description:
• New: History for any app. Right-click an app and choose History… to see its last 7, 30 or 90 days: processor, memory, energy and network over time, how long it was in front, its crashes and alerts, and the hours of the week it's busiest.
  • New: Slowdowns you missed. Why is my Mac slow? now also lists the times in the last 7 days your Mac struggled, with when, how long, and the apps busiest then. Click an app to see its history.
  • New: What happens after you log in. Startup shows how long your Mac took to calm down after its last startup and which apps kept it busy, marking the ones that open with your Mac. Checkup mentions it when a login keeps the Mac busy for 5 minutes or more. (Mactivity needs to open at login to see this.)
  • About and Settings show just the version, like "1.0.2", without the build number.
  • Claude Code shows the Claude icon instead of a blank square, and so does any helper app that ships without an icon of its own.
  • Click any app in a history chart's Top apps list to open its history.

item.title: Mactivity 1.0.1
item.description:
• The toolbar button that explains what's slowing your Mac is now called Diagnose. Hover over it for the full question.
  • Bluetooth accessories like a Magic Keyboard or Trackpad are listed once, not twice, using the name you gave them.
  • The Battery tab shows accessories in their own card, with a level bar for each, beside the Mac's own power and heat figures.
  • The menu bar window's bottom row never cuts off a label: it says "Quit" and "Open" when the full names don't fit.
  • About shows "Version 1.0", no longer "1.0 beta".

item.title: Mactivity 1.0
item.description:
• Mactivity is out of beta: a license is $10, once, for three Macs, at mactivity.app/buy, with a full refund within 14 days if it isn't for you.
  • New: Runaway process alerts. When a node, python or similar process sits at a full core for 10 minutes, or its memory keeps climbing, Mactivity tells you which one, which project it belongs to and which coding agent started it. Quitting it is one confirmation away; Mactivity never stops anything on its own.
  • New: SSD health. The Disk tab shows each drive's own report: how much of its rated life is used, how much it has written, and whether it reports any trouble. Checkup speaks up when a drive wears out or reports a problem.
  • New: Reports. Save the last 7 or 30 days as a two-page PDF from View → Save Report or History's Your week card: the figures, a day-by-day chart, the busiest hour and the apps behind it, and the top apps by every measure.
  • New: Slow drift in Checkup. Checkup notices an app whose memory has crept up over the past weeks, and a battery that empties faster than it used to.
  • Keep Awake is now called Stay Awake.
  • Ask Mactivity is now off unless you switch it on in Settings → General, and it says plainly that its answers should be checked against the figures.
  • A project with many listening ports no longer pushes the menu bar window's Projects page off screen.
  • The Battery tab's period switch turns into a menu when the labels don't fit, as in German.
  • Agents: Stop now also ends the shells a Claude Code session starts in their own process groups.
  • Browser breakdown: Chromium's network service is recognized, and an Electron app's main process is labelled correctly.
  • Recordings are saved in full when you quit during one, and a write that fails says so.
  • "Unplugged at" finds the right time even after more than a day on battery.
  • Clearer wording throughout the app and the website.

item.title: Mactivity 0.9.7.2
item.description:
• New: Agents. Track your AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Aider and more) in their own sidebar tab: each session's project, the app it runs in, its running time, and the processor and memory taken by it and everything it launched. Stop… ends a whole session after you confirm, and leaves the app or terminal it runs in alone.
  • New: Why is my Mac slow? One click, in the toolbar, the menu bar window, or Quick Search, explains in plain words what's slowing your Mac right now: an app hogging the processor, memory running short, heat, a full or busy disk, a busy graphics processor, Low Power Mode, or macOS's own background work like Spotlight indexing, Time Machine, Photos, iCloud or an update. Each cause has a button to quit the app or see the details.
  • New: Quick Search. Press ⌃⌥M anywhere to search apps, processes and ports, like ":3000". Return shows the result in Mactivity, and ⌘⌫ quits it after asking. Change it in Settings → General.
  • New: Keep Awake. The cup at the foot of the menu bar window, or View → Keep Awake, holds off sleep for 1, 2 or 4 hours or indefinitely, and can keep the display lit as well. It lets go on its own if the battery gets low or the Mac heats up.
  • New: mactivity mcp. Coding agents such as Cursor, Codex and Claude Code can now check on the Mac themselves: what's busy, what's slowing it, which dev servers and agent sessions are up. It can only read. Settings → Command Line copies the line that adds it to Claude Code.
  • New: Record Activity. View → Record Activity… (⌥⌘R) saves every second's figures, for the Mac and each busy app, to a CSV file until you stop it or an hour passes.
  • New: Since unplugged. While you're on battery, the Battery tab can show which apps have used it since the Mac came off its charger, and at what time that happened.
  • New: Browser breakdown. Expand Safari, Chrome or another Chromium browser and its tab processes, extensions, GPU process and network service each get a line, with their portion of the total. Electron apps break down into windows and helpers.
  • New: Your connection. The Network tab shows the interface, your local IP address, the router, and Wi-Fi signal, speed and channel.
  • New alerts: free space on the startup disk below an amount you choose (10 GB to start), your Mac running hot for 5 of the last 10 minutes (with the app working hardest), and, if you turn it on in Settings → Alerts, a lost connection.
  • New: Apps open but unused. Checkup lists apps you haven't used for days that still hold memory, with a Quit… button for each.
  • New: Hotspot data watch. On your iPhone's hotspot, the Network tab shows how much data each app has used since you connected, and Mactivity alerts you when an app uses a lot in a short time. You can change the amount, or turn it off, in Settings → Alerts.
  • New: Ask Mactivity. Type a question into Quick Search, such as "why is my fan loud?" or "which app drained my battery yesterday?", and Apple Intelligence answers on your Mac using its figures and history. Your question never leaves the Mac. Available where Apple Intelligence is turned on.
  • Settings → General shows which version you have, beside Check for Updates….
  • The Battery tab's list covers the last 24 hours or 7 days, rolling. Plugged in, it shows how the energy divided up between apps instead of an empty list; with time on battery, how the battery did.
  • Disk totals are right from the moment Mactivity opens, not only after five minutes.
  • Checkup and crash alerts ignore crashes of an app's older versions once you've updated it.
  • Storage → Messages Attachments… frees space taken by old Messages photos and videos on this Mac. Pick by age, kind and size, and they go to the Trash. The messages, and everything on your iPhone, stay.
  • Storage → Clean Up → iPhone and iPad Backups… shows Finder's backups of your devices, and downloaded iPhone and iPad updates, with their sizes, and moves the ones you tick to the Trash.
  • Checkup mentions Messages attachments older than a year and device backups older than six months, when they take real space.
  • Storage → Clean Up → Installers and Archives in Downloads… finds disk images, installers and archives left after installing, and downloads that never finished, and moves the ones you tick to the Trash.
  • Storage shows the space you can get back, cleanup by cleanup, and what's still in the Trash, with a Review button for each.
  • Storage → Clean Up → Mail Downloads… finds copies of attachments Mail saved when you opened them.
  • Settings → Privacy shows whether Mactivity has Full Disk Access, what it's for, and how to turn it on.
  • Checkup mentions a Trash holding over 5 GB.
  • Storage → Clean Up → Developer Caches… frees Xcode DerivedData and package-manager caches that rebuild themselves.
  • Checkup tells you when a macOS update is waiting to install.
  • Onboarding mentions Full Disk Access, for Storage's cleanups, when it's off.
  • The menu bar icon no longer flickers when memory pressure hovers at the warning line.
  • Storage → Clean Up → Screenshots and Screen Recordings… finds old captures on your Desktop and in your screenshot folder, in any language, and moves the ones you tick to the Trash.
  • Storage → Clean Up → Purgeable Space… explains purgeable space, removes downloads of iCloud files you pick (they stay in iCloud), and lists local Time Machine snapshots. Click Purgeable in the disk's legend to open it.
  • When your startup disk is close to capacity, Checkup says how much Storage → Clean Up can recover.
  • The mactivity command shows network use per app, and mactivity top --network sorts by it. Shortcuts' Top Apps has it too when macOS has just opened Mactivity for it.
  • The welcome screen offers to open Mactivity at login (ticked), so its history has no gaps.
  • If Mactivity opened long after your Mac started and isn't set to open at login, Checkup says history has a gap and points to the setting.
  • Growing-memory alerts measure from the app's typical memory at the start of the hour, so one bad reading after the Mac wakes can't make a steady app look like it grew.
  • "Your Mac stayed awake last night" no longer fires after a night asleep with Power Nap's short wakes, and Checkup no longer says so either.
  • Startup tags an empty plist "Empty", not "Broken": some updaters (Google's) empty theirs to switch off. It no longer counts as starting with your Mac, or as broken in Checkup.
  • Time on battery no longer counts time asleep: a day in a bag with Power Nap read as 24 hours. Past days are corrected when you update.
  • A Quit… confirmation now shows only where you asked for it, not also in the app list behind a sheet.
  • A process that starts with the ID of one that just ended no longer reads as 0 MB for its first second.
  • Hotspot data keeps counting across a sleep or a dropped connection, instead of starting again from zero.
  • Apps open but unused never suggests quitting Mail, Messages, Slack, Music and other apps people keep open for notifications or playback, or an app that's busy right now.
  • Growing-memory alerts come back once an app has released its memory, instead of staying silent until it passes its old peak.
  • High CPU, heavy disk and heavy network alerts need the whole window of readings: a busy minute before sleep and a busy second after waking no longer count as 10 busy minutes.
  • Quiet hours follow your Mac to a new time zone.
  • The daily summary goes out even if your screen stays on all morning, and the weekly summary goes out later in the week if your Mac was off on Monday.
  • The uninstaller only ever moves the app you picked and its own files in your Library, whatever its Info.plist says.
  • Space you can get back updates right after a cleanup.
  • Messages and Mail cleanups judge age by when the file arrived, not when it was last edited.
  • Screenshots cleanup keeps working after you change where screenshots are saved.
  • You can move files to the Trash from a Startup Disk map in Storage.
  • Mail Downloads lists a Pages or RTFD attachment as one item.
  • History keeps working after the clock is set ahead and back, and keeps the last minutes before a long shutdown.
  • The year calendar's daily figures weigh each hour by how much of it was recorded.
  • History's days follow a time-zone change without relaunching.
  • Your week's average sleep no longer counts an afternoon nap as a night.
  • Compare with the previous period says when there isn't enough history, instead of comparing against an hour of it.
  • Right after your Mac wakes, apps' CPU shows correctly instead of all of it landing under macOS for a moment.
  • The mactivity command and Shortcuts show GPU use per app.
  • A download by a short-lived command (curl, brew) now counts toward its app's network use.
  • Background services caught at the moment they start no longer show as "xpcproxy" under macOS for good.
  • Quick Search's selection stays on the app you picked while the list updates, and macOS's own processes can't be quit from it.
  • Checkup's idle dev servers and Quick Search's ports are always current.
  • Apps open but unused only lists apps Mactivity has actually seen go unused, and updates after you quit one.
  • Why is my Mac slow? says when it has nothing to go on yet, instead of "All clear".
  • A Keychain that can't be read for a moment (a declined password prompt) no longer loses your license, and entering your key again never uses another seat.
  • A proxy or captive portal's error page during the weekly license check no longer deactivates Mactivity.
  • Activation says when you're not really online, instead of showing "HTTP 200".
  • Mactivity unlocks as soon as it's back online after a month offline, not hours later.
  • Stopping a dev server never stops the editor, REPL or terminal that started it.
  • Homebrew services (Postgres, Redis) are no longer shown as a dev project or stopped by Stop Idle.
  • Docker containers show when OrbStack or Colima is running, even if Docker Desktop left an old socket behind.
  • Stop All stops every server at once instead of one after another.
  • Widgets show a big change within 15 minutes, as intended, instead of up to 30.
  • A project with many listening ports (a Cloudflare Workers setup can hold 16) no longer breaks the menu bar window's Projects page. Rows show the first port and how many more, and every port is in the tooltip.

item.title: Mactivity 0.9.7
item.description:
• Checkup is where you already look: its summary sits on Overview and in the menu bar window, which also says when an app is keeping your Mac awake and shows your accessories' battery levels.
  • Checkup tells you when Mactivity's notifications are turned off, since every alert and the weekly summary depend on them.
  • Power by app now measures each app's own energy. It read close to zero before.
  • On the power adapter, Power draw shows what your Mac is drawing instead of 0, and Source names the adapter's wattage.
  • Energy Impact lists show each app's share as a percentage, and the Now / Today / 7 days switch stays on the right.
  • Disk totals count everything since your Mac started up, even from before Mactivity began recording, and say "at least" where history doesn't reach back far enough. Read and write counts are short and readable ("35.3M reads").
  • Totals over a month or a year (data written, data used, time on battery) no longer overcount hours your Mac slept through part of.
  • History's charts always span their whole range, and no longer flatten your data under a far-off alert line.
  • Overview's cards fill every row on wide windows.
  • Apps are grouped better: the iOS Simulator's helpers count as Simulator, Xcode's device services as Xcode, and app extensions like Excel's widget as their app.
  • Fewer false alarms: crash alerts and Checkup count crashes of apps, not of command-line tools and test helpers; Checkup no longer suggests quitting parts of macOS; and a "keeps using more memory" alert repeats only once the app has grown again.
  • Your week says when time in use started recording, instead of calling a few hours a whole week.

item.title: Mactivity 0.9.6
item.description:
• No more keychain password prompts: Mactivity keeps your license in a part of the keychain that belongs to the app, so it never has to ask. The first launch moves it over, asking at most once if macOS insists.
  • Share makes an image of Overview's cards with their live graphs. Send it from the Share menu, copy it, or save it to Downloads.
  • The year at a glance: History opens with a calendar of the last year, one square per day, for CPU, GPU, memory, disk or network. Click a day to see its hours and its busiest apps.
  • Export History… in Settings → History saves every hour kept, for every app, as a CSV file for a spreadsheet.
  • Accessories: History shows the battery of your AirPods, Magic Mouse, Keyboard and Trackpad over time, when each was last charged, and about how long it has left.
  • History keeps your Mac's battery level (with how many times it charged), memory pressure, swap, and free space, with a forecast of when the disk will be full at the current rate. Data used shows how much each app sent and received.
  • Sleep: see what's keeping your Mac awake right now (also on the Battery tab), a week of when it slept, and what woke it.
  • The Disk tab shows data read and written since startup, today, this week, this month and this year, the read and write counts, and which apps wrote the most today.
  • Crashes and hangs per app, from macOS's own reports on your Mac, and time in front: how long you used each app.
  • New alerts: an accessory battery low, the disk filling up, an app that keeps crashing, and a Mac that stayed awake all night. Each can be turned off in Settings → Alerts.
  • Checkup: a short list of what's worth doing on your Mac, from a filling disk to an app that keeps crashing, each with a button to fix it.
  • Battery use by app, like the iPhone's: switch the Battery tab's list to Today or 7 days to see what used your battery, plus battery health and when it'll reach 80%.
  • The Battery tab's chart shows your battery level, and says how much you used and charged ("Used 90%, charged 60%"). Top apps show each app's share of energy.
  • Your week: time in use, sleep, data and crashes for the last seven days, as a card on History, a shareable image, and a Monday notification.
  • Uninstall App… in Storage moves an app and the files it left in your Library to the Trash, after showing you everything first.
  • Fixed: top apps ranked apps that ran for a few seconds, like Phone, above apps used all day.

item.title: Mactivity 0.9.5
item.description:
• Mactivity now needs a license: $10 once, for up to three of your Macs. Until you paste your key, the window and the menu bar show only the license screen, and nothing is sampled or recorded. Licenses are by invitation during the private beta.
  • A year of history. Mactivity keeps 15-minute detail for 30 days and hourly detail for a year, and History adds 90-day and 1-year ranges. A year takes about 40 to 60 MB; change it in Settings → History.
  • At 30 days, the busiest apps show how they moved against the 30 days before.
  • Search finds processes and PIDs too, not just apps.
  • Hover a figure like Wired, Compressed or Load average to see what it means.
  • Mute an app's alerts from its row, or from the notification itself.
  • Right-click a dev server to open it in your browser, in Terminal or in Finder, or copy its URL.
  • Storage: press Space for Quick Look, ⌘⌫ to move the selected item to the Trash, ⌘R to rescan, or drag an item into Finder.
  • VoiceOver reads chart summaries. With Differentiate Without Color on, statuses are shown as words.

item.title: Mactivity 0.9.4
item.description:
• Quit, Force Quit, stopping a dev server, disabling a startup item and Move to Trash work again: confirming the dialog did nothing.
  • Storage rows show Show in Finder and Move to Trash buttons when you point at them, no right-click needed.
  • After Move to Trash, Mactivity reminds you the space comes back when you empty the Trash.
  • The Storage list no longer fills empty space with striped rows.

item.title: Mactivity 0.9.3
item.description:
• Temperatures in Celsius or Fahrenheit: Settings → General → Temperature. Automatic follows your Mac's region.
  • Energy Impact no longer spikes when short-lived processes start (Xcode builds read as tens of thousands).
  • The Battery tab's history says it's showing Energy Impact, with whole numbers on the axis.
  • Week and month charts no longer show the same date twice.
  • Battery time remaining uses the battery's own estimate, which isn't capped at 20 hours.
  • Percentages follow your region's style, like "27 %" in Germany and France.
  • Choose what each metric shows in Settings → General → Figures: memory as used, percent or pressure; network as download, upload or both; disk as free space, percent used or activity; battery as percent, time left, both or watts; and which temperature sensor. Automatic keeps today's figures.
  • Hide rows you don't need in the menu bar window: Settings → Menu Bar → Menu bar window.
  • A Process menu with keyboard shortcuts: Get Info ⌘I, Show in Finder ⇧⌘R, Quit ⌥⌘Q, Force Quit ⌥⌘⌫, plus Quit and Get Info buttons in the toolbar. Mactivity still asks before quitting anything.
  • Mactivity tells you when notifications are off, with a button to turn them on.
  • A Storage scan now survives switching tabs.
  • Desktop Macs get an Energy tab instead of an empty Battery tab.
  • "Volume" in the sidebar is now "Sound". Clicking the Dock icon opens the window.
  • Mactivity speaks your language: German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Dutch, Japanese, Korean, and Chinese (Simplified and Traditional). It follows your Mac's language setting. These translations are new; tell us about anything that reads oddly.
  • Lighter: about 12% less CPU while idle in the menu bar, faster history charts, and the menu bar window and Settings let go of their views when closed.

item.title: Mactivity 0.9.2
item.description:
• GPU sits next to CPU everywhere: the sidebar, the menu bar window, Overview, History, and the menu bar picker.
  • Click an app in the menu bar window to open it in Mactivity, highlighted on that tab.
  • Share cards carry the Mactivity icon.
  • Every metric tab lines up exactly: no more jumping when you switch tabs in the menu bar window or the main window.
  • Rows, columns and headers line up throughout: labels and values in the menu bar window, History's titles, tags, and the storage map, which no longer resizes as you hover it.

item.title: Mactivity 0.9.1
item.description:
• The toolbar shows the history range and search only on the tabs they change.
  • Startup shows an item's details in an inspector you can hide.
  • The menu bar window's buttons use Liquid Glass.
  • With Increase Contrast on, status dots, card edges, warning tags and the storage map are easier to see.
  • Storage's Map, Categories, Developer and Largest Files switcher sits in the toolbar.
